climate.overview_html: The UN Climate Summit 2026 closed on September 24 with the following headline commitments: the United Kingdom pledged £330 million to the Global Environment Facility for nature-based solutions and climate adaptation; Australia and Turkey were confirmed as COP31 co-hosts, with COP31 scheduled for Antalya, Turkey, November 9–20, 2027; and 47 nations joined the “35 by 35” electrification pledge committing to 35% clean electricity in all end-use sectors by 2035. Carbon Brief’s quarterly state-of-climate analysis, published today September 25, finds 2026 on track as the second-warmest year on record at approximately 1.51°C above the pre-industrial baseline — and places a 92% probability on 2027 becoming the warmest year ever recorded at approximately 1.71°C, driven by the ongoing Super El Niño peak propagating into NH winter. The physical backdrop that anchors both findings: the Copernicus C3S bulletin published September 10 confirmed August 2026 as the world’s joint-hottest month on record at 16.96°C global-mean surface temperature — 1.65°C above the 1850–1900 pre-industrial baseline — the first month to exceed the 1.5°C Paris Agreement threshold since November 2025, with western Europe’s JJA 2026 registering as the continent’s hottest summer on record.

items.source: UN News / Climate Change News / France 24
items.headline: UN Climate Summit 2026 Closes September 24: UK Pledges £330 M to GEF; COP31 Confirmed Antalya, Turkey, November 9–20, 2027 (Australia–Turkey Co-Hosts); 47 Nations Join “35 by 35” Electrification Pledge; Finance Framework: $1.3 Trillion/Year by 2035
items.summary: The UN Climate Summit 2026 concluded on September 24 with several headline commitments. The United Kingdom pledged £330 million to the Global Environment Facility for nature-based solutions and climate adaptation. COP31 was confirmed for Antalya, Turkey, November 9–20, 2027, with Australia and Turkey as co-presidents — resolving the host uncertainty that had persisted since early 2026. Forty-seven nations endorsed the '35 by 35' electrification pledge committing to 35% clean electricity across all end-use sectors by 2035. The summit's finance framework called for total climate finance flows of $1.3 trillion per year by 2035, with at least $300 billion per year for developing nations — a target feeding directly into UNFCCC NCQG negotiations ahead of COP31.

items.headline: Carbon Brief State of Climate Q3 2026 (September 25): 2026 Tracking Second-Warmest Year on Record at ~1.51°C Above Pre-Industrial; Super El Niño Drives 92% Probability 2027 Becomes Warmest Year at ~1.71°C; Jan–Aug 2026 Anomaly 0.25°C Above 2023 at Same Point
items.summary: Carbon Brief's quarterly state-of-climate analysis, published September 25, finds the January–August 2026 period tracking 1.51°C above the 1850–1900 pre-industrial baseline — approximately 0.25°C warmer than 2023 at the same point in the year. The current Super El Niño peak, with its Niño 3.4 daily anomaly reaching 3.07°C, is the primary driver. Looking ahead, the analysis places a 92% probability on 2027 becoming the warmest year on record at a central estimate of 1.71°C above pre-industrial — the highest annual mean ever modelled — reflecting the well-documented 4–8 month lag between El Niño SST peak and global-mean temperature response. The finding is consistent with WMO's September–November 2026 forecast placing Niño 3.4 at approximately +3.6°C and projecting above-normal temperatures for most global land areas through NH winter.

items.headline: Copernicus C3S August 2026 Bulletin: Joint-Hottest Month on Record at 16.96°C Global-Mean Surface Temperature (1.65°C Above 1850–1900 Pre-Industrial) — First Month >1.5°C Paris Threshold Since November 2025; Western Europe JJA 2026 Hottest Summer on Record
items.summary: The Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S) reported on September 10 that August 2026 tied with August 2023 as the hottest August on record at 16.96°C global-mean surface temperature — 1.65°C above the 1850–1900 pre-industrial average. This makes August 2026 the first calendar month to exceed the 1.5°C Paris Agreement threshold since November 2025, following a brief return to sub-1.5°C conditions during NH winter and spring 2026. For western Europe specifically, the June–August 2026 period was the hottest summer on record, with France, Spain, Germany, and Portugal all recording their highest June–August mean temperatures. The anomaly is driven primarily by Super El Niño's SST contribution plus the long-term warming trend; 12 of the previous 13 months had been the warmest on record for their respective calendar months.

items.headline: Carbon Brief Analysis: Super El Niño Daily Niño 3.4 Anomaly Hit 3.07°C on September 19 — Near-Tie with All-Time Daily Record (3.08°C, 19 Nov 2015) but Two Months Earlier in Calendar; August Monthly Anomaly 2.45°C; Further Strengthening Forecast
items.summary: Carbon Brief analysis using NOAA daily SST data finds the Niño 3.4 daily anomaly reached 3.07°C on September 19, 2026 — placing it in a statistical tie with the previous all-time daily record of 3.08°C from 19 November 2015. Critically, the 2026 record arrived approximately two months earlier in the seasonal calendar, while official forecasts continue to indicate further strengthening through October–December 2026. August 2026 had a monthly Niño 3.4 anomaly of approximately 2.45°C — higher than the peak of every prior El Niño on record except 2015–16 and the 1877–78 event. Further strengthening to a new all-time record is expected before the seasonal peak in December–February.

items.headline: Super El Niño Multi-Model Forecast: 75% Probability of Strongest Event on Record Since 1950; OND 2026 Median Peak +2.67°C; 90%+ Probability Super El Niño Persists September–January; Spring 2027 Neutral Transition 55%
items.summary: Updated NOAA CPC and IRI multi-model ensemble forecasts give a 75% probability that the current Super El Niño will surpass the 1997–98 event to become the strongest on record since 1950. Median OND 2026 forecast is +2.67°C for the Niño 3.4 index. There is a 90% or greater probability of the Super El Niño phase persisting through September 2026–January 2027. A 55% probability of returning to neutral phase by April–June 2027 is consistent with historical post-Super El Niño patterns. NOAA projects a median peak of approximately 4.1°C in December — about one degree higher than the record-breaking 2015–16 event's peak.

items.headline: WMO Global Seasonal Climate Update SON 2026: Niño 3.4 ~+3.6°C; Positive IOD +0.9°C; Above-Normal Temperatures Forecast for Most Land Areas; 2027 Still Forecast as Warmest Calendar Year on Record
items.summary: WMO's Global Seasonal Climate Update for September–November 2026 places the Niño 3.4 index at approximately +3.6°C above average, consistent with the Super El Niño at or approaching its seasonal peak. The co-occurring positive Indian Ocean Dipole at +0.9°C amplifies drought risk over Indonesia, the Philippines, and eastern Australia while increasing rainfall risk over eastern Africa and the Horn. Above-normal temperatures are forecast for most global land areas in SON 2026. WMO confirms 2027 remains the likely warmest calendar year on record as the El Niño peak contribution propagates into NH winter 2026/27.

items.source: Geophysical Research Letters / AGU / PIK Potsdam
items.headline: GRL Vol. 53 Issue 17: “Global Warming Has Accelerated Significantly” — Foster & Rahmstorf; First Statistically Confirmed Acceleration Since ~2015 at >98% Confidence; Fastest of Any Decade in 177-Year Record Across Five Temperature Datasets
items.summary: Foster and Rahmstorf apply natural-variability filtering across five global temperature datasets (NASA GISTEMP, NOAA GlobalTemp, HadCRUT5, Berkeley Earth, ERA5) to isolate the forced warming signal from ENSO, volcanic, and solar variability. The residual shows, for the first time with greater than 98% statistical confidence, that global warming has accelerated since approximately 2015 at a rate faster than any previous decade in the 177-year record. The result directly strengthens the attribution basis for the Nepal–Tibet UNFCCC Loss and Damage Fund submission active at UNGA.

weather.overview_html: The dominant operational development: INVEST 91W was upgraded to Tropical Storm Surigae — JTWC designation 25W, PAGASA name Tropical Storm Queenie — entering the Philippine Area of Responsibility on September 24 as the 25th named system of the 2026 West Pacific typhoon season; as of the 5 am PAGASA forecast, Surigae was approximately 1,535 km east-northeast of extreme northern Luzon, tracking west-northwest at 15 km/h with sustained winds of 65 km/h and gusts to 80 km/h; PAGASA does not forecast a direct Philippines landfall, and JMA’s operational guidance indicates typhoon-intensity attainment is possible by September 27. In the Atlantic: the 2026 season’s zero-hurricane streak has now extended at least 7 days beyond the previous satellite-era record of September 18, 1966; all six named storms reached only tropical storm intensity, with Super El Niño’s wind shear confirmed as the primary attribution. In Southeast Asia: the Philippines health advisory remains active as haze from more than 300,000 ha of Indonesian fires reaches Metro Manila; ASEAN Level 3 alert continues and CAMS’s Mark Parrington expects deterioration through October as El Niño suppresses the Indonesian wet-season onset.

items.headline: Tropical Storm Surigae (JTWC 25W) / “Queenie” (PAGASA) UPDATED September 24: Enters Philippine Area of Responsibility 1,535 km East of N. Luzon; Winds 65 km/h Gusts 80; WNW Track at 15 km/h; No Philippines Landfall Forecast; Typhoon Intensity Possible September 27
items.summary: INVEST 91W was upgraded to Tropical Storm Surigae (JTWC designation 25W, PAGASA name Tropical Storm Queenie) on September 24, 2026, entering the Philippine Area of Responsibility. The 5 am PAGASA forecast placed Surigae approximately 1,535 km east-northeast of extreme northern Luzon, tracking west-northwest at approximately 15 km/h, with maximum sustained winds of 65 km/h and gusts of up to 80 km/h. JTWC post-genesis intensity analysis confirmed sustained winds of approximately 40 knots. Environmental conditions remain favorable: wind shear below 15 knots and warm SSTs of 29–30°C. JMA's operational forecast indicates the possibility of typhoon-intensity attainment by September 27. PAGASA's current track forecast shows no direct landfall over any Philippine island, with the storm tracking north of the main Philippine archipelago toward the East China Sea.

items.source: Wikipedia / ABC News / Al Jazeera / SANA
items.headline: Nepal–Tibet Floods UPDATED: Missing Toll Raised to ~6,150 on September 16 (Up From ~3,916); ~1,400+ Confirmed Dead in Nepal and Tibet Combined; Rehabilitation Phase Ongoing; UNFCCC Loss and Damage Submission at UNGA
items.summary: Nepal's government raised the official missing persons count from approximately 3,916 to approximately 6,150 on September 16, 2026. The confirmed death count stands at approximately 1,400 across Nepal and Tibet combined. The event was triggered on August 26 by a glacier collapse on Langtang Lirung that produced catastrophic debris flows along a 72 km stretch of the Trishuli River; seismometers recorded Ms 5.2 tremors. Nepal's UNFCCC Loss and Damage Fund submission, citing the Foster & Rahmstorf GRL warming acceleration result, is active at UNGA.

items.headline: 2026 Atlantic Hurricane-Free Streak Extends Through September 25: Record for Longest Hurricane-Free Run in Satellite Era (Post-September 18, 1966) Now Extended >7 Days Beyond Previous Record; Super El Niño Wind-Shear Attribution Confirmed
items.summary: The 2026 Atlantic hurricane season's streak of zero hurricane formations extends through at least September 25, now more than 7 days beyond the previous satellite-era record of September 18, 1966. Tropical Storm Fay became post-tropical on September 23 without reaching hurricane intensity. The season's six named storms (Alex through Fay), all at tropical storm strength or below, reflect Super El Niño-driven vertical wind shear across the main development region. NOAA forecasts indicate the below-normal pattern will persist through at least October as the Super El Niño continues to strengthen.

items.source: Mongabay / CAMS / Philstar / Asian News Network
items.headline: SE Asia Wildfire Haze UPDATED September 24: Philippines Government Health Advisory Issued; >300,000 ha Burned in Indonesia; 12 Million+ People Across Six Countries Blanketed; ASEAN Level 3 Alert; Smoke Could Persist Through October
items.summary: The Philippine government has issued a formal health advisory as haze from Indonesian fires reaches Metro Manila, adding a sixth nation to the affected zone. More than 300,000 hectares have burned across Borneo and Sumatra per Nusantara Atlas data. CAMS senior scientist Mark Parrington warned that if fire emissions continue to increase as expected through September into October, smoke and air quality impacts could persist for several weeks. Indonesia's Health Ministry recorded 113,336 respiratory infection cases across seven provinces as of September 9. The ASEAN Level 3 (highest) haze alert remains active. Conditions are consistent with the worst Indonesian fire season in 11 years, driven by Super El Niño-suppressed late rainy season onset.

items.headline: Pakistan Monsoon Flood Death Toll UPDATED: 907 Dead / 1,044 Injured Nationwide Since Late June Per NDMA (September 6 Figure); Flash Flooding Ongoing in Sindh, KPK, GB, Punjab; Final Monsoon Active Phase
items.summary: Pakistan's NDMA as of September 6, 2026 reported 907 dead and 1,044 injured across the country since monsoon onset in late June. House collapses account for approximately 48.6% of fatalities; drowning and flash flooding are the other leading causes. The worst-affected provinces remain Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Punjab. Urban flooding has inundated parts of Lahore, Rawalpindi, and Faisalabad. Approximately 2 million homes have been damaged or destroyed and an estimated 1 million livestock have perished. The final monsoon active phase extends through late September.

renewables.overview_html: Fluence announced on September 24 a multi-year battery supply framework with EVE Energy covering 206 GWh of utility-scale energy storage systems from 2027 through 2031 — one of the largest long-term BESS supply commitments in the industry, securing EVE-3 cylindrical cell technology at scale ahead of anticipated demand growth. WindEnergy Hamburg 2026 closed on September 25 after four days with more than 1,600 exhibitors and 43,000 participants from 100 countries; the dominant policy theme from Day 4 was grid-code harmonization for floating offshore wind, following RWE’s September 22 call for Europe-wide CfD indexation. The largest asset deal of the recent window: Enel’s $760 million acquisition of an 810 MW US solar portfolio (525 MW Faraday Utah + 100 MW Skyhawk Tennessee) generating approximately $90 million annual EBITDA. IEA’s 2026 energy investment outlook projects global clean energy investment reaching $2.2 trillion in 2026, with grid investment approaching $550 billion.

items.headline: Fluence — EVE Energy 206 GWh Multi-Year Battery Supply Framework 2027–2031 — September 24: Utility-Scale BESS Systems; EVE-3 Cylindrical Cell Technology; One of Largest Long-Term BESS Supply Commitments in Industry; ~5 GW of Estimated Projects
items.summary: Fluence, the energy storage technology and services company jointly owned by Siemens and AES, announced on September 24 a multi-year battery supply framework agreement with EVE Energy covering 206 GWh of utility-scale battery energy storage systems from 2027 through 2031. The deal secures supply of EVE's new EVE-3 large-format cylindrical cell technology, offering improved energy density and cycle life versus earlier flat-plate formats. Fluence will deploy the cells in its Gridstack and Ultrastack BESS platforms. The 206 GWh five-year commitment covers approximately 5 GW of estimated projects and is one of the largest long-term BESS supply frameworks disclosed in the utility-scale storage industry. EVE Energy had disclosed the framework agreement from its side on September 18; Fluence's September 24 confirmation provided the technology and deployment detail.

items.source: PV Magazine USA / Renewable Watch / Mercom Capital
items.headline: Enel Closes $760 Million Acquisition of 810 MW US Solar Portfolio from Excelsior Energy Capital; 525 MW Faraday Utah (Meta Off-Taker, 20-Year PacifiCorp PPA) + 100 MW Skyhawk Tennessee (TVA PPA); ~$90 Million Annual EBITDA
items.summary: Italian energy major Enel completed the acquisition of an 810 MW portfolio of US solar assets from Excelsior Energy Capital at an enterprise value of approximately $760 million, closing on or around September 11, 2026. The portfolio consists of the 682 MW DC (525 MW AC) Faraday solar plant in Utah County backed by a 20-year PacifiCorp PPA with Meta as off-taker, and the 127 MW DC (100 MW AC) Skyhawk plant in Tennessee backed by a TVA PPA. Combined assets generate approximately $90 million per year in EBITDA. The deal is part of a broader $1.3 billion wind and solar agreement; the remaining 205 MW wind capacity is expected to close Q4 2026.

items.headline: RWE at WindEnergy Hamburg September 22: Calls for Europe-Wide CfD Indexation for Offshore Wind; Up to €4.4 Billion in Savings for Germany’s 9 GW Pipeline by 2030; €2 Billion Potential Savings for 4 GW Tendered in 2027
items.summary: RWE's head of offshore wind development called at a NedZero panel at WindEnergy Hamburg on September 22 for Europe-wide adoption of indexation for offshore wind Contracts for Difference. The mechanism — already implemented in the UK and Belgium — links contract strike prices to inflation indices over the operating term. For Germany's 4 GW planned for tendering in 2027, potential cost reductions are estimated at up to €2 billion; for Germany's full 9 GW tender pipeline through 2030, the figure rises to up to €4.4 billion.

items.headline: CTUIL Releases TSA for 2 GW Solapur Renewable Energy Evacuation and Transmission Expansion Project (India) — Selected Bidder Gets 10-Day Window to Execute Agreement and Acquire 100% SPV Equity
items.summary: Central Transmission Utility of India Ltd (CTUIL) released a Transmission Service Agreement on September 23, 2026, for a 2 GW renewable energy evacuation and transmission expansion project in Solapur, Maharashtra. Following issuance of the Letter of Intent, the selected bidder will have 10 days to execute the TSA and pay the acquisition price for 100% equity in the Special Purpose Vehicle. The project is part of India's grid reinforcement program to evacuate power from the Solapur solar and wind zones — a critical bottleneck for India's 500 GW renewable target by 2030.

items.headline: 50Hertz Awards LanWin3 2 GW North Sea HVDC Converter Platform to NSORe + Siemens Energy — Second 2 GW NSORe/50Hertz Contract in 2026; Combined LanWin3 + LanWin6 Value ~€2.5 Billion
items.summary: German TSO 50Hertz awarded the LanWin3 North Sea offshore HVDC converter platform contract to the Neptun Werft–Smulders Offshore Renewables (NSORe) JV and Siemens Energy on September 18. This is NSORe's second major 50Hertz contract in 2026, following LanWin6 in June. Siemens Energy supplies the high-voltage components; NSORe handles design, procurement, construction, offshore installation, and commissioning. Combined NSORe value for LanWin3 and LanWin6 totals approximately €2.5 billion.

items.headline: LS Marine Solution Wins 156.9 Billion Won (~US$114 M) Submarine Cable Contract for 390 MW Sinan Wooi Offshore Wind Farm — South Korea’s First National Growth Fund Project; Largest-Ever LS Marine Order; First in 8.2 GW Sinan Belt
items.summary: LS Marine Solution secured a 156.9 billion Korean won (~US$114 million) contract on September 18 to supply and install submarine power cables for the 390 MW Sinan Wooi offshore wind farm — its largest-ever order at 2.2 times its full-year FY2025 revenue. Sinan Wooi is the first project to receive funding from South Korea's National Growth Fund for offshore wind, and marks the opening project in the government-designated 8.2 GW Sinan offshore wind development belt. Cable installation is scheduled 2026–2028.

science.overview_html: The most operationally significant new paper: Landsberg and Barnes (Geophysical Research Letters, September 24, Colorado State University) find that current operational AI weather models — including ECMWF AIFS, GraphCast, and Pangu-Weather — inherit a systematic cold bias of approximately 0.035°C/decade from ERA5 reanalysis training data, equivalent to 15–20 years of warming; naive comparison of AI model 2-m temperature forecasts against present-day observations will therefore understate warming bias and corrupt climate attribution use cases unless explicitly corrected. Two new ocean emulation papers extend the AI geoscience frontier: HClimRep-Ocean (arXiv:2609.28601, September 23) introduces the first transformer ocean emulator on FESOM2’s unstructured mesh, achieving full 3D reconstruction of temperature, salinity, SSH, and sea ice with state-of-the-art skill versus ClimaX and FourCastNet ocean baselines; and Neptune (arXiv:2609.08606, September 8) demonstrates a CNN + Spherical Fourier Neural Operator hybrid that outperforms SFNO-only and persistence baselines at 2–6-week ocean S2S lead times, including the first AI-model AMOC 26°N skill score (r > 0.6 at 4 weeks). Continuing from the operational ML NWP stream: WeatherNext 3 (Google DeepMind, September 3) and AICON (DWD, August 25) remain the current benchmarks for hourly 0.1° satellite-assimilating forecasting and high-resolution operational NWP respectively.

items.source: Geophysical Research Letters / AGU / Colorado State University
items.headline: GRL: AI Weather Model 2-m Temperature Forecasts Carry 15–20-Year Cold Bias From ERA5 Training Data — Landsberg & Barnes (CSU / GRL 2026); ~0.035°C/Decade Systematic Underestimate in ECMWF AIFS, GraphCast, Pangu-Weather; Bias Correction Required Before Climate Attribution
items.meta: Landsberg & Barnes · Colorado State University · Geophysical Research Letters (2026) · doi:10.1029/2025GL119740 · Published 24 September 2026
items.summary: Landsberg and Barnes evaluate 2-metre temperature forecasts from three leading AI weather models — ECMWF AIFS, Google DeepMind GraphCast, and Huawei Pangu-Weather — and identify a systematic cold bias of approximately 0.035°C per decade inherited from the ERA5 reanalysis training corpus. Because ERA5 spans 1940–2024, its mean temperature reflects a background state approximately 15–20 years of global warming prior to the present day; models trained on ERA5 climatology produce 2-m temperature anomalies calibrated against a cooler baseline. Evaluated against WMO station data for 2021–2025 hindcasts, all three models show consistent negative temperature bias growing with forecast lead time. The study concludes these models are unsuitable for near-real-time climate attribution or warming-trend estimation without explicit post-processing bias correction, and calls for training dataset refreshes or dynamic climatology normalization as standard practice. The finding directly complicates use of AI weather model output as a proxy for observed temperature trends.

items.headline: HClimRep-Ocean (arXiv:2609.28601) — First Transformer Ocean Emulator on FESOM2 Unstructured Mesh; Full 3D Reconstruction Including Sea Ice, Salinity, SSH; State-of-the-Art vs. ClimaX and FourCastNet Ocean Baselines at 1–12-Month Horizons
items.summary: HClimRep-Ocean introduces the first transformer-based ocean emulator designed to operate on FESOM2's native unstructured triangular mesh, avoiding the regridding artifacts introduced when existing transformer ocean models map irregular ocean grids to structured latitude–longitude grids. The architecture uses hierarchical climate representation with multi-scale attention operating at coarse, medium, and fine resolution levels. Variables include 3D temperature and salinity at 24 depth levels, sea surface height, and sea ice concentration and thickness. Evaluated on multi-decadal hindcasts against FESOM2 reference runs, HClimRep-Ocean achieves state-of-the-art skill scores versus ClimaX ocean fine-tune and FourCastNet ocean baselines across all variables at 1–12-month prediction horizons. The unstructured-mesh capability is particularly significant for accurately representing coastal upwelling zones and polar ocean processes that govern long-range climate prediction skill.

items.headline: Neptune (arXiv:2609.08606) — CNN + SFNO Hybrid Architecture for Global Ocean Sub-Seasonal-to-Seasonal Prediction; NEMO4 Training; Outperforms SFNO-Only and Persistence at 2–6-Week Lead Times; First AI-Model AMOC 26°N Skill (r > 0.6 at 4 Weeks)
items.summary: Neptune combines a convolutional neural network backbone for capturing local mesoscale features with a Spherical Fourier Neural Operator (SFNO) for learning global-scale teleconnections, trained on NEMO4 ocean model output covering 1958–2020. The CNN-SFNO hybrid significantly outperforms SFNO-only and persistence baselines at 2–6-week prediction horizons for sea surface temperature, mixed layer depth, and upper-300m heat content. Skill is strongest for Atlantic AMOC-influenced SST patterns and Pacific ENSO-forced SST. Neptune is the first AI ocean model to demonstrate skillful S2S prediction of the AMOC 26°N array index, with correlation skill r > 0.6 at 4-week lead times — a metric of direct relevance to European climate prediction and extreme weather risk.

items.headline: WeatherNext 3 (arXiv:2609.03582) — Google DeepMind + Google Research: Operational Hourly Global Probabilistic Forecasts at 0.1° via Raw Geostationary Satellite Ingestion; Functional Generative Networks on Multiresolution Icosahedral Mesh; Powers Google Search + Google Maps
items.meta: Google DeepMind + Google Research · arXiv:2609.03582 [cs.LG] · Submitted 3 September 2026 · Operational
items.summary: WeatherNext 3 generates new probabilistic forecasts every hour by ingesting low-latency geostationary satellite imagery directly, achieving 0.1° spatial resolution — on par with operational physics-based global models — while eliminating the 6-hour analysis lag that constrains traditional AI model architectures. Architecture: Functional Generative Networks with an encode-process-decode structure operating on a multiresolution icosahedral mesh. WeatherNext 3 is now operationally deployed by Google, currently powering weather data in Google Search and Google Maps.

items.headline: AICON (arXiv:2608.24651) — DWD’s Operational Global ML Weather Model at 13 km, 3-Hour Step; GNN Encoder-Processor-Decoder on Icosahedral Multi-Mesh; Trained on High-Resolution ICON-DREAM Dataset; Operational Since March 2, 2026
items.meta: Deutscher Wetterdienst (DWD) et al. · arXiv:2608.24651 [physics.ao-ph] · Submitted 25 August 2026 · Operational at DWD since 2 March 2026
items.summary: AICON is the German national meteorological service's operational global machine learning weather prediction model, generating forecasts at 13 km spatial resolution with a 3-hour time step. Architecture: a graph neural network with an encoder-processor-decoder structure using graph attention for node updates, operating on an icosahedral multi-mesh derived from ICON's native grid. AICON avoids autoregressive multi-step rollout during training, prioritizing small-scale fidelity. AICON entered full operational use at Deutscher Wetterdienst on March 2, 2026, making DWD one of the first national meteorological agencies to operationalize a purpose-built ML NWP model at high resolution.

items.headline: FAST-ML: Hybrid Physics–ML Framework for Tropical Cyclone Intensity Forecasting (arXiv:2609.25505) — Dual-Stream ERA5 Neural Parameterization Coupled to Differentiable FAST Intensity Model; End-to-End Optimization; Rapid Intensification Forecast
items.meta: Xiao, Lin, Ehrmann, Sarhadi · arXiv:2609.25505 [physics.ao-ph] · Submitted 22 September 2026
items.summary: FAST-ML bridges data-driven efficiency with physical constraints for tropical cyclone intensity forecasting, specifically targeting rapid intensification. A physically-informed dual-stream neural parameterization ingests 3D ERA5 atmospheric fields to diagnose two key ventilation controls: environmental vertical wind shear and the mid-level entropy deficit. These parameters are fed into a differentiable implementation of the FAST intensity model, with parameters optimized end-to-end. By embedding physical constraints directly into the learning objective, FAST-ML ensures storm evolution remains governed by thermodynamic principles while benefiting from neural network flexibility. Directly relevant to TS Surigae (25W) intensity guidance.

items.headline: Sparse-Observation Atmospheric Thermal Forecasting With Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Climate-Aware Digital Twins (arXiv:2609.27290) — Chegini et al.; RMSE Improvement 8.1% at 1-Hour to 23.8% at 3-Hour Lead vs. Baselines; Oklahoma ERA5 Case Study
items.meta: Chegini, Shivanian, Karimi, Dadgostari · arXiv:2609.27290 [physics.ao-ph] · Submitted 23 September 2026
items.summary: Evaluates a physics-informed neural network constrained by a pressure-coordinate thermodynamic advection–source equation for short-horizon (1–3 hour) atmospheric temperature forecasts at sparse-observation locations. The PINN achieves mean RMSE improvement over persistence and local-trend baselines growing from 8.1% at one hour to 23.8% at three hours in an Oklahoma development case. The result supports climate-aware digital twin use cases for built-environment operations, smart grids, and wildfire risk platforms requiring hyperlocal thermal forecasts in data-sparse regions.

items.headline: From Regional to Global: Transfer Learning for Atmospheric Transport Emulators (arXiv:2609.23838) — Clark et al. (U Bristol); LPDM Emulator Extended from South America to Four Global Regions; ~1,000× Faster Than Physics-Based Model; Enables High-Resolution Satellite GHG Inversion at Scale
items.meta: Clark, Fillola, Keshtmand, Santos-Rodriguez, Rigby · arXiv:2609.23838 [physics.ao-ph] · Submitted 20 September 2026 · University of Bristol
items.summary: Evaluates whether a high-performance Lagrangian Particle Dispersion Model emulator previously developed for South America — running approximately 1,000× faster than the UK Met Office's NAME LPDM — can be spatially transferred to new regions via transfer learning. The authors evaluate transferability across four world regions using region-specific and multi-region models, establishing conditions under which transfer learning extends the emulator without full retraining. The result opens a pathway toward global, high-resolution greenhouse gas inversion from modern satellite instruments (OCO-2, TROPOMI) at costs previously achievable only for regional domains.

items.headline: TAISE: AI-Driven Catastrophe Risk Modeling via Emergent Scenario Generation (arXiv:2609.16493) — Hang Gao; 50-Year Simulation on One GPU for US$130 with 2,000+ Cyclonic Events; Order-of-Magnitude Cost Reduction vs. Traditional CAT Models
items.summary: TAISE repurposes AI weather forecasting models to generate coherent continuous global atmospheric fields via self-iterative rollout, from which extreme events emerge rather than being manually constructed. A proof-of-concept 50-year simulation on a single GPU cost approximately US$130 and produced more than 2,000 cyclonic events — an order-of-magnitude reduction in computational cost versus conventional catastrophe modelling. The framework captures temporal continuity and cross-regional correlations absent in snapshot-based CAT model approaches. Directly applicable to the reinsurance/ILS sector, which has seen five consecutive years of insured nat-cat losses exceeding US$100 billion.

items.headline: Nature Climate Change: Heat-Related Labor Productivity Loss = US$41/tonne CO<sub>2</sub> (90% CI $1–108) — Moore, Haqiqi, Kong et al.; Second-Largest SC-CO<sub>2</sub> Component After Heat Mortality; Agricultural Damage Revised Down to $29/tonne Using AR6
items.meta: Moore, Haqiqi, Kong et al. · Nature Climate Change (2026) · doi:10.1038/s41558-026-02749-z · Published 16 September 2026
items.summary: Moore, Haqiqi, Kong et al. quantify heat-related labor productivity loss as a standalone social cost of carbon component, finding a central estimate of US$41 per tonne CO₂ (90% CI $1–108) — the second-largest SC-CO₂ component after heat mortality. Agricultural damage was simultaneously revised down from US$95 to US$29 per tonne CO₂ using IPCC AR6 methods and updated dose-response functions. Losses are geographically concentrated in South Asia, East Asia, Southeast Asia, and Sub-Saharan Africa. Immediate implications for climate damage assessments used in litigation and regulatory cost-benefit analysis.

items.headline: Nature Communications: Hunga Tonga Stratospheric Aerosol Layer Catalysed CH<sub>4</sub> Oxidation at 900±220 Mg/day Via Cl-Radical Pathway — 12 ppb HCHO at 30 km; Pathway Absent From All CMIP7 Models; Implications for SAI and Large-Eruption Scenarios
items.meta: van Herpen et al. · Nature Communications (2026) · doi:10.1038/s41467-026-72191-4 · Published 15 September 2026
items.summary: Van Herpen et al. show that the 2022 Hunga Tonga eruption's stratospheric sulphate aerosol layer catalysed a previously uncharacterised methane oxidation pathway involving Cl radicals produced at aerosol surfaces. CH₄ oxidation is quantified at 900 ± 220 Mg/day between 25–35 km, explaining the anomalous HCHO column of ~12 ppb at 30 km (~8× background). The mechanism is absent from current CMIP7 chemistry–climate models; if triggered by large eruptions or proposed stratospheric aerosol injection, it could constitute a net cooling offset not captured in climate sensitivity assessments or geoengineering scenario modelling.

items.title: NOAA NESDIS Awards $67 Million to Spire Global, PlanetiQ, and Ethereal Space for Commercial GNSS-RO Data — 10,000 Daily Radio-Occultation Profiles for NWP and Space-Weather Monitoring; Multi-Year Operational Contracts Through 2029
items.body_html: NOAA’s National Environmental Satellite, Data, and Information Service announced on September 18 awards totalling $67 million to three commercial GNSS radio-occultation providers — Spire Global, PlanetiQ, and Ethereal Space — for operational data contracts running through 2029. The contracts will deliver approximately 10,000 radio-occultation soundings per day, nearly doubling the operational GNSS-RO input to NOAA’s Global Forecast System and ECMWF-based NOAA products. PlanetiQ’s GNOMES constellation contributes high-precision tropospheric refractivity profiles; Spire Global’s LEMUR network provides distributed low-Earth orbit coverage; and Ethereal Space, in its first NOAA operational contract, provides specialized polar-orbit coverage relevant to Arctic sea-ice and polar vortex monitoring — direct inputs to the AI weather models tracked in the Science & Research section above.

items.title: Fortune / PitchBook: Climate Tech VC Fund Fundraising Fell ~40% in H1 2026 Despite Record Investment Totals — AI Data Centre Demand Filling Gap Left by Pure-Climate Funds; Bifurcation Sharpening Between AI-Adjacent and Traditional Climate-Only Verticals
items.body_html: Fortune, citing PitchBook LP fundraising data, reported on September 23 that climate-tech-dedicated VC fund formation fell approximately 40% in H1 2026 by capital raised compared to H1 2025 — even as total climate-tech investment reached a record $26.1 billion in the same period per CTVC’s separate deal-level tally. The paradox reflects a structural shift: AI-infrastructure demand for firm low-carbon power (nuclear, geothermal, long-duration storage) is increasingly funded by generalist and growth funds that do not self-identify as “climate VC” — bypassing the dedicated climate fund layer. PitchBook’s analysis finds that the 10 largest H1 2026 climate deals drew on sovereign wealth funds, Big Tech corporate VC, and pension capital rather than dedicated climate GPs — a bifurcation that could hollow out early-stage climate pipeline if LPs continue to withdraw from pure-play climate fund vehicles.

items.title: Kairos Power Secures Up to $100 Million from Samsung C&T for Google Hermes 2 Nuclear Reactor Build — $70 M Equity + $30 M In-Kind Engineering; 50 MW Fluoride Salt-Cooled Demonstration Plant at Oak Ridge; Operations Target 2030
items.body_html: Kairos Power and Samsung C&T agreed on September 21 to a binding term sheet under which Samsung C&T will provide up to $100 million — $70 million in direct equity plus $30 million in in-kind engineering and procurement services — to support the delivery of Kairos’s 50 MW fluoride salt-cooled, high-temperature reactor (KP-FHR) Hermes 2 Demonstration Plant in Oak Ridge, Tennessee. Hermes 2 is purpose-built to supply firm low-carbon baseload power for Google’s AI data centres under a previously announced clean-power purchase agreement; Samsung C&T brings direct reactor construction execution capability across approximately a dozen nuclear projects globally. The investment is subject to regulatory approvals and scheduled for completion in 2030.
items.source_html: TechCrunch / World Nuclear News

items.title: Rainmaker Raises $100 Million Series B for Drone-Based Cloud Seeding — Led by NOA VC + Upfront; DCVC, Lowercarbon, Dream Ventures Co-Invest; Pitches Cloud Seeding as Adaptation Tech for Data Center Water Demand and Drought Relief
items.body_html: Rainmaker, the El Segundo, California weather-modification startup, announced a $100 million Series B on September 21 led by NOA VC and Upfront Ventures with co-investment from DCVC, Lowercarbon Capital, and Dream Ventures — bringing total funding to $150.3 million since its 2023 founding. Rainmaker deploys custom drone fleets to seed clouds with silver iodide or other nucleating agents; the company frames cloud seeding as climate adaptation rather than geoengineering, targeting drought relief in the American West and cooling and humidification services for water-hungry hyperscale data centers. The round will fund atmospheric research team expansion, drone fleet development, and commercial trials in the Southwest.
items.source_html: Fast Company / PR Newswire

items.title: CTVC / Currence H1’26 Climate Tech Report: $26.1 Billion Global VC in H1 2026 (+55% YoY); Data Centers 34% of Total; Deal Count at 5-Year Low (-25%); Series A up 55% to $4.5 Bn; Adaptation Funding +64% — Fastest-Growing Sub-Vertical
items.body_html: CTVC (now Currence) published its H1’26 Climate Tech Investment & Innovation Report on September 21, 2026, finding total global venture investment reached $26.1 billion in H1 2026 — up 55% year-on-year and the strongest first half since 2022 — driven overwhelmingly by data-centre infrastructure. The Built Environment category grew more than 800% and overtook Energy as the largest funding vertical, with the “speed-to-power race” driving data-centre developers toward low-carbon firm power sources — advanced nuclear, superhot geothermal, long-duration storage — as gas turbine lead times stretch to 5–8 years. Deal count fell 25% to a 5-year low; the 10 largest rounds took 42% of all H1 2026 investment. Series A rose 55% to $4.5 billion on nuclear appetite; adaptation funding grew 64% — the fastest-growing sub-vertical.

items.title: Cat Bond and ILS Market Bulletin (Week Ending September 20): MembersCap Launches First Cat Bond Fund + Novel ILW; Gallagher Securities Developing First-Ever New-Peril Cat Bond; CalPERS ILS Holdings Approach US$2.5 Billion — Fifth Consecutive Year of >$100 Billion Global Insured Nat-Cat Losses
items.body_html: The Artemis weekly bulletin for the week ending September 20, 2026 highlights three developments in the catastrophe bond and ILS market: MembersCap launched the first dedicated cat bond fund strategy alongside a novel industry loss warranty (ILW) structure designed to expand ILS investor access; Gallagher Securities is developing the first-ever cat bond covering a previously unbondable peril, representing a structural expansion of the cat bond market’s risk frontier; and CalPERS’ insurance-linked securities holdings are approaching US$2.5 billion at mid-year 2026, cementing its position as the largest institutional investor in the cat bond asset class — all in the context of the fifth consecutive year of global insured natural catastrophe losses exceeding US$100 billion.

items.title: Mazama Energy Raises $135 Million Series B for Superhot Engineered Geothermal — Led by Centaurus Capital + Doerr Capital; ConocoPhillips, Shell Ventures, Khosla, Gates Frontier Co-Invest; Project Athena Targeting 750°F (400°C) at Newberry Volcano, Oregon
items.body_html: Mazama Energy raised $135 million in an oversubscribed Series B announced September 17, co-led by Centaurus Capital (John Arnold’s fund) and Doerr Capital. ConocoPhillips, Shell Ventures, Khosla Ventures, Gates Frontier, SiteGround Capital, H. Barton Asset Management, and the Jeffrey and Marieke Rothschild Foundation also participated. Mazama holds the record for the hottest EGS ever built — a 629°F (331°C) well at Newberry Volcano in 2025; Project Athena targets 750°F (400°C), where a single well can deliver up to 10× the power of a conventional 390°F well using 75% less water and 80% fewer wells.

items.title: EU Climate Insurance Alliance — Von der Leyen State of the Union September 16: Only 25% of European Catastrophe Losses Currently Insured; Parametric + Group Instruments Proposed; 100 Vulnerable EU Regions Mapped by October; Alliance Faces Criticism for Lacking Mandatory Cover Mandate
items.body_html: European Commission President von der Leyen announced the European Climate Insurance Alliance in her September 16 State of the Union address, citing data showing only 25% of European catastrophic climate losses are currently insured. The Alliance will develop group insurance pools for currently uninsurable catastrophe risks and expand parametric instruments for agriculture, coastal flooding, and wildfire; the European Commission will map the 100 most-vulnerable EU regions by October 2026. The announcement follows Europe’s wildfire season reaching 668,035 ha per EFFIS, with uninsured losses estimated at €40–60 billion. Critics noted the Alliance would not close the protection gap without mandatory natural-hazard cover.
items.source_html: Green Central Banking / The Insurer

items.title: Laki Power Raises €6 Million Series A Led by NATO Innovation Fund — Iceland Grid Monitoring Device Self-Powered From Live HV Lines; NIF’s First Iceland Investment; + ReykVC
items.body_html: Laki Power, a Reykjavík-based grid monitoring hardware company, closed a €6 million Series A on September 16 led by the NATO Innovation Fund with co-investment from ReykVC — NIF’s first investment in an Icelandic company. Laki Power’s core product harvests its operating power directly from live high-voltage transmission lines via inductive energy harvesting, eliminating external power supplies and batteries; the device provides real-time line-current, temperature, sag, and fault-location data — directly relevant to Nordic and Arctic grid resilience and NATO dual-use energy security.
